newsitem.title: UK: UK funds show similar returns amid fewer managers.
newsitem.headline: UK funds show similar returns amid fewer managers.

text.p: A concentration of pension fund assets under fewer and fewer investment managers may be leading to reduced variation in investment performance, performance measurement agency CAPS said.

It said that in 1996 UK pension funds showed an overall median return of 10.8 percent, with only a 2.2 percentage point range between the upper and lower quartile returns of 12 and 9.8 percent respectively.
The range was the lowest since formal performance measurement began in 1970, it said.

"This, allied to the current situation where there are fewer and fewer investment managers in control of pension fund assets, poses the question -- Are they all doing the same thing in terms of investment?."
CAPS said the use of stock selection was again the key to under- and outperformance of funds in 1996.

The year's best performing sectors were UK, European and US equities, it said, and over the year funds took money out of the two best performing sectors (UK and U.S. equities) at a time when they were both producing the best results.
CAPS in 1996 measured 3,047 portfolios, representing 1,620 funds with a total value of 269 billion sterling.
It measures over half of the segregated pension funds in the UK.
